title: ibook2epub library export
description: A reader's library taken out of Apple Books: what they own, who wrote it, when they got it, and the collections they sorted it onto. A catalogue rather than a reading history. Measured against a real 3,620-book library, the rating, page count, year and finished columns are empty on every row and eleven books carry a finish date, so every field beyond title, author, collections and acquisition date is present only when the database holds it.

$schema.description: Optional pointer back to this schema.

version.description: The version of ibook2epub that wrote the file.

generated.description: When the file was written, UTC, seconds precision, always ending in Z.

books.description: Every book in the library, by title.

title.description: As Apple recorded it. Falls back to the asset id when Apple recorded none.

author.description: As Apple recorded it, or as the book's own package document declares it when Apple recorded none.

authorSort.description: The author's sort name, 'Corey, James S. A.', as the package document declares it through opf:file-as. Apple keeps no such column, so it is present only when the package document was read and declares one.

year.description: The year Apple recorded. Null on every row of a surveyed library, so usually absent.

identifier.description: The publication's own dc:identifier, rendered canonically exactly as the annotation export renders it: a verifiable ISBN becomes 'urn:isbn:' and thirteen digits, a UUID becomes lowercase 'urn:uuid:', anything else is left as declared. Present only when the package document was read and declares something usable. Not unique: 52 books in a surveyed library share theirs with another.

declaredIdentifier.description: The identifier exactly as declared, present only when canonicalising changed it.

source.description: Name of the package directory or file Apple holds the book in, e.g. 'Leviathan Wakes.epub'. The path is deliberately not recorded: it names the reader's home directory.

filename.description: Name of the file on the shelf, under the naming policy the run was using. Absent when the run named no policy.

assetId.description: Apple's identifier for the book. Unique within the library, stable across a re-export, and what the annotation export joins on.

added.description: When the book entered the library, UTC, from ZPURCHASEDATE: set on every row of a surveyed library including sideloaded books, and spanning the life of the library. Not ZCREATIONDATE, which dates the database row -- it begins in mid-2025 for a library going back to 2016.

lastOpened.description: When the book was last opened, UTC.

finished.description: When the reader finished the book, UTC. Eleven of 3,620 books carry one in a surveyed library.

progress.description: How far through the book the reader is, as a share of it: 1 is the end. Absent when the book has not been started.

rating.description: The reader's rating, when Apple recorded one. Zero on every row of a surveyed library, so usually absent.

pages.description: The page count, when Apple recorded one. Zero on all but one row of a surveyed library, so usually absent.

collections.description: Every collection the book is in, sorted, exactly as named in Books. Includes the ones Apple fills itself -- Library, Downloaded, Books, PDFs, Audiobooks -- which the CSV leaves out because they describe storage and format rather than shelving.

shelf.description: The reading state the evidence supports: 'read' on a finish date, a finished flag, or progress at the end of the book; 'currently-reading' on progress short of it. Absent when the database says nothing, which is most books. Never 'to-read': that is an assertion about intent the database cannot support, and the CSV makes it only when --unknown-shelf asks for it.
